description: The order model gained a `discount_cents` column and the migration for it was never written. `alembic.ini` says this project manages its database with Alembic, `alembic/versions/` is in the project and holds no revision, so a database created before the change is never brought up to the shape `app/models.py` describes.

required_outcomes.title: `alembic.ini` says Alembic is in use in this project, and `alembic/versions`, where Alembic keeps the record of how the database reached its shape, is here and holds no migration.
required_outcomes.why: `alembic/versions/` exists and holds no `.py` revision, which is the exact state the check calls Confirmed at MustFix. The two evidence anchors are `alembic.ini` and `alembic/versions`, both AnchorSubject::Database, and neither carries an excerpt of a project line.

This is the one fixture in P14 whose detector already reaches the severity the release manifest names: MustFix blocks hand-off on its own, and crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts both the severity and the evidence bar behind it.

The same project with one `.py` revision under `alembic/versions/` must make no claim at all. The control project is built in crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs, so a check that answered MustFix to every Alembic project cannot pass this fixture's tests.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The project is reported as working, verified or passing while `alembic/versions/` holds no migration and the model has moved on from any database that exists.
The project aggregates to green on the strength of the fixture's own check. That check builds a fresh database from the model on every run, so it is green whatever the migration directory holds.
The empty record is not reported at all, and the missing migration is left to be discovered by whoever runs the deployment.
A project that has an Alembic revision is reported as missing one. The control project in crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs fails if that happens.

notes: Severity: unlike every P14-T001 fixture, this one has no gap to record. evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json asks for must_fix and the check produces MustFix, critical, EvidenceClass::ObservedFact, so nothing here is filed as style noise by false_completion_aggregator::is_style_noise. What is narrower than the manifest's wording is the claim itself, and it is recorded rather than hidden: the manifest case reads `schema change without required migration identified`, and nothing in a path listing records a *change*. What SURE detects is the checkable coarser fact - a project that writes down the shape of its database and keeps no record of how it got there. A project whose migrations exist but do not cover a model added last week is not detectable here; see the module documentation of crates/sure-core/src/db_migrations.rs. This fixture holds the `must_fix` shape and not the other one: `alembic/versions/` is present and empty, which is Confirmed at MustFix, whereas a project with no versions directory at all is Confirmed at ShouldFixFirst. That choice is frozen in crates/sure-core/tests/db_migrations.rs and recorded in progress/DECISIONS.md. Runnable with `python`, standard library only, no network, no writes: the app builds an in-memory SQLite database and never opens a file on disk.
